'''''Rumex bucephalophorus''''', also known as horned, red, or ruby dock is an annual herbaceous plant that is part of the family [[Polygonaceae]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250060773|title=Rumex bucephalophorus in Flora of North America @ efloras.org|website=www.efloras.org|access-date=2019-10-03}}</ref> The scientific name ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' was first described and published by [[Carl Linnaeus|Linnaeus]] in 1753 in ''[[Species Plantarum]].''<ref name=":0" /> Other scientific names have also been given to ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' such as ''Bucephalophora aculeata'' and ''Lapathum bucephalophorum''.<ref name=":0" /> ''R. bucephalophorus'' is most commonly found in subcoastal or coastal regions, but also are "casual aliens", few and far between, among inland populations.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Talavera|first=Maria|date=December 2011|title=Molecular phylogeny and systematics of the highly polymorphic Rumex bucephalophorus complex (Polygonaceae)|journal=Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution|volume=61|issue=3|pages=659–70|doi=10.1016/j.ympev.2011.08.005|pmid=21864695}}</ref> ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' is native to the [[Mediterranean Basin]] and grows best in areas with little human intervention.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Talavera|first=María|date=12 July 2012|title=Evolution of dispersal traits in a biogeographical context: a study using the heterocarpic Rumex bucephalophorus as a model|journal=Journal of Ecology|volume=100|issue=5|pages=1194–1203|doi=10.1111/j.1365-2745.2012.01999.x|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Description ==
The stems of ''R. bucephalophorus'' are thin and branch off the base of the plant about 5 to 50 centimeters long. The leaves of the plant vary as they can be circular and [[Ovate (botany)|ovate]] or lengthened and [[Lanceolate|lancelate]] anywhere in between.<ref name=":0" /> The pedicels are known to be heteromorphic often distinguishing this plant from others.<ref name=":0" />  Flowers are often found in groups of 2 to 3 in clusters and are also often heteromorphic.<ref name=":0" /> Like its leaves, the flowers of ''R. bucephalophorus'' often vary greatly but are generally triangular and 2–4 mm long.<ref name=":0" />

The ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' flowers appear red and blossom between the months of December and May.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Rumex+bucephalophorus|title=Rumex bucephalophorus red dock PFAF Plant Database|website=pfaf.org|access-date=2019-10-03}}</ref>

== Distribution ==
The genus ''Rumex'' is mostly distributed throughout North America and Europe.<ref name=":2" /> However, ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' flourishes in habitats that are quite sandy and rocky therefore it often is found by the sea''.<ref name=":1" />'' The Atlantic coast of southwestern Europe, the northwestern region of [[Macaronesia]] and [[Morocco]], and the coastlands of the [[Mediterranean Basin]] are where ''R. bucephalophorus'' is most widely distributed.<ref name=":2" />

== Subspecies ==
''Rumex bucephalophorus'' is unique as it is a [[Polymorphism (biology)|polymorphic]] species resulting in 8 different [[subspecies]] as well as dozens of variants and subvariants.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tropicos.org/Name/26001923?tab=subordinatetaxa|title=Tropicos {{!}} Name - Rumex bucephalophorus L.|website=www.tropicos.org|access-date=2019-10-03}}</ref>

* ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' ssp. ''aegaeus''
* ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' ssp. ''bucephalophorus''
* ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' ssp. ''canariensis''
* ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' ssp. ''graecus''
* ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' ssp. ''fruticescens''
* ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' ssp. ''gallicus''
* ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' ssp. ''hipporegii''
* ''Rumex bucephalophorus'' ssp. ''hispanicus''

== Uses ==
''R. bucephalophorus'' does not have any known uses, but it is an edible plant.<ref name=":1" /> There is a danger, however, because its leaves contain a high level of [[oxalic acid]] that can be potentially dangerous in large amounts.<ref name=":1" /> This [[oxalic acid]] gives the leaves an acid-lemon flavor.<ref name=":1" />
